tagline: See exactly how a slicer selection travels through your data model

slides.title: How a Slicer Filters Your Data
slides.body: When you select a value in a slicer, Power BI propagates a filter through the model via relationships. Understanding exactly where that filter travels — and where it stops — is essential for correct DAX and safe model design.
slides.keyPoint: Filters travel from the ONE side (dimension) to the MANY side (fact table). They do NOT travel in reverse by default. This is single-direction cross-filtering.

slides.title: Step 1 — Base Star Schema, No Filters Active
slides.caption: Four tables connected by three 1:M relationships. All data visible, no slicers selected.

slides.title: Step 2 — User Selects Category = 'Bikes'
slides.caption: Filter enters via DimProduct and flows down the 1:M relationship into FactSales. DimDate and DimRegion are unaffected.
slides.filterNote: Category = 'Bikes' restricts FactSales to Bike rows only. DimDate and DimRegion are unaffected — single-direction filtering stops at the fact table.

slides.title: Why Doesn't the Filter Reach DimDate or DimRegion?
bullets: Default cross-filter direction is SINGLE: filters flow from the ONE side (dimension) to the MANY side (fact) — not backwards.
DimDate and DimRegion are also ONE-side tables. Filters from DimProduct cannot jump across FactSales to reach them.
This is intentional: it prevents one slicer from inadvertently filtering another dimension's available values.
Result: COUNTROWS(DimDate) = 365 regardless of the Category slicer — dates are never reduced by a Product filter.
Exam: 'Why does the Region slicer still show all regions when Bikes is selected?' — Single-direction filtering. Regions are unaffected.
slides.keyPoint: In a star schema with single-direction filtering, each dimension is independently filterable. A filter on one dimension never propagates to another dimension through the fact table.

slides.title: Step 3 — Bidirectional Filter Enabled (Dangerous)
slides.caption: Enabling BOTH cross-filter direction lets filters flow fact → dimension. DimRegion now shows only regions where Bikes were sold.
slides.filterNote: Bikes filter flows DimProduct → FactSales → DimRegion. The Region slicer now only shows regions that sold Bikes.
slides.issue: Bidirectional filtering can bypass Row-Level Security. If FactSales has an RLS filter, it may propagate back into DimProduct, exposing dimension values that should be restricted.

slides.title: Bidirectional Filter — When to Use and When to Avoid
bullets: Use SINGLE direction in almost all star schema designs. It is safe, predictable, and performant.
Use BOTH only when a dimension slicer must dynamically show only values that exist in the fact data — a specific, intentional UX choice.
Never enable BOTH when the model has Row-Level Security. Bidirectional can propagate security filters in unexpected directions, exposing restricted data.
Performance cost: BOTH doubles query plan complexity — VertiPaq must evaluate filter paths in both directions simultaneously.
Exam trap: 'After enabling bidirectional filtering, the Region slicer shows fewer options than expected.' This is correct and expected behavior.
slides.warning: Default to SINGLE cross-filter direction. Enable BOTH only with full understanding of its security and performance impact.
